title: How the retrieval layer learns: inscription, genericization and entity collapse
description: These claims hold how the retrieval layer treats what is deposited into it: SPXI as Concept (#671) holds that it learns the entity rather than about it, the Hexagonal Licensing Protocol (#66, #1182) that it dissolves generic descriptions, the Fortification Protocol (#173) that it merges a provenanced term into a higher-frequency neighbour, and #673 that it prefers the better-structured, more widely dispersed definition. They run through the Thornburgh and Feist Function disambiguation packets and the r.27 Internet room, with forecasts (#1268, #517) that platform erasure will not stop summarizer indexing, and a few unbuilt tests such as the Feist/Feistel probe sentence and quarterly Encyclotron snapshots. The page also holds six unrelated claims, among them the sex binary and a Sappho 31 reconstruction level.
